routes.name: Visa-free visit (British citizens, 180 days)
routes.summary: British citizens can visit Hong Kong without a visa for up to 180 days. Entry is not automatic and officers can refuse it.

sources.label: ImmD visit visa and entry permit requirements

routes.name: Visa-free visit (90 days list)
routes.summary: Citizens of the US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, South Korea, Singapore, Malaysia, Brazil, Mexico, Israel, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, Kenya and most EU/EEA countries and Switzerland get 90 days visa-free. See the official list for every country.

other: Covers most EU/EEA states, Switzerland, the Americas listed by ImmD, Australia, NZ, Japan, Korea, Singapore, Malaysia and others. Check the official list for your passport.

sources.label: ImmD visit visa and entry permit requirements

routes.name: Visa-free visit (30, 14 and 7 day lists)
routes.summary: Some nationalities get 30 days (for example UAE, Thailand, Indonesia, South Africa, Qatar, Peru), others 14 days (for example India with pre-arrival registration, Russia, Philippines, Ukraine, Kazakhstan, Mongolia). Other foreign nationals not on a visa-required list get 7 days.

other: India needs pre-arrival registration. Albania and Serbia only with biometric passports.

sources.label: ImmD visit visa and entry permit requirements

stay.note: 30 days for the 30-day list, 14 days for the 14-day list, 7 days for other nationals not requiring a visa.

routes.name: Visit visa
routes.summary: Nationals of countries such as Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Iran, Nigeria, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Vietnam and others on the official list need a visa before visiting. Apply through the nearest Chinese embassy or consulate (Indian applicants apply directly to ImmD).

other: Applies to nationalities on the official visa-required list. Stateless travel document holders also need a visa.

sources.label: ImmD visit visa and entry permit requirements

routes.name: Transit (airside) rules
routes.summary: Most travelers can transit by air without a visa if they stay in the airport transit area. Nationals of some countries (for example Afghanistan, Iran, Iraq, Nigeria, Somalia, Syria, Yemen, and others) need a visa even for airside transit. Check the official list.

other: You usually need an onward or return ticket, except when transiting to Mainland China or Macao.

sources.label: ImmD visit visa and entry permit requirements

routes.name: General Employment Policy (GEP)
routes.summary: Work visa for skilled people with a confirmed job offer in Hong Kong that locals can't readily fill. Quota-free.

eligibility.education: Normally a first degree in a relevant field
other: Pay should match the market for HK professionals.
Mainland residents use the ASMTP instead.
Overseas Chinese PRC passport holders may qualify under facilitation measures.

stay.note: Initial stay normally 36 months or contract length. Extensions usually 3 years then 2. Top-tier stream (HK$2 million assessable income after 2 years) can get 5 years.

routes.processing: About four weeks after all documents and fees are received.
documents: Employer: contract or offer letter, business registration, financial standing proof

routes.name: Admission Scheme for Mainland Talents and Professionals (ASMTP)
routes.summary: Work route for Chinese Mainland residents with a job offer in Hong Kong. Quota-free and not limited to any sector.

eligibility.education: Normally a first degree in a relevant field
other: For Mainland Chinese residents only.
Pay should match the HK market.

stay.note: Initial stay normally 36 months or contract length. Extensions usually 3 then 2 years. Top-tier stream can get 5 years.

routes.processing: About four weeks after all documents and fees are received.

routes.name: Top Talent Pass Scheme (TTPS)
routes.summary: No job offer needed. Apply as a high earner (Category A), an experienced graduate of an eligible university (B) or a recent graduate (C, with a yearly quota). You can work or run a business without prior approval.

income.note: Category A, in the year before applying, from taxable employment or business

other: Category B: eligible university graduate with 3+ years of work in the past 5 years.
Category C: eligible university graduate in the past 5 years with under 3 years of work. Yearly quota, first come first served.

stay.note: Initial stay 36 months for Category A, 24 months for B and C. Extensions normally up to 3 years. Top-tier stream can reach 6 years.

routes.processing: About four weeks for new applications, two to three weeks for extensions.

routes.name: Quality Migrant Admission Scheme (QMAS)
routes.summary: Points-based route with no job offer needed. Pass the General Points Test or the Achievement-based Points Test for exceptional people.

eligibility.education: Normally a first degree from a recognized institution
other: General Points Test passing mark is currently 6 out of 12 and can change without notice.
Must support yourself and dependants without public assistance.

stay.note: General test: 36 months then usually 3+2 years. Achievement-based: normally 8 years. Holders with 2+ years in HK and HK$2 million assessable income can apply for a 5 year top-tier extension.

routes.name: Immigration Arrangements for Non-local Graduates (IANG)
routes.summary: Stay and work after graduating from a Hong Kong institution or a jointly run Greater Bay Area campus. Apply within 6 months of graduating and you need no job offer.

eligibility.education: Full-time undergraduate or higher degree from an authorized HK institution or GBA joint campus
other: Apply later than 6 months after graduation and you need a degree-level job offer at market pay.
Nationals of Laos, Nepal and Vietnam are limited to certain UGC-funded programs plus GBA campus graduates.

stay.note: Initial stay usually 24 months. Extension needs a qualifying job offer or proof of business. Top-tier stream can get 6 years.

routes.name: New Capital Investment Entrant Scheme (New CIES)
routes.summary: Investor route. Hold at least HK$30 million in net assets for 6 months, then make HK$30 million of permissible investments. InvestHK certifies both steps before ImmD approves.

investment.note: Net, in permissible investment assets, on top of net assets of at least HK$30 million held for 6 months

savings.note: Net assets held for 6 months before applying

other: Open to foreign nationals, Chinese nationals with overseas permanent residence, Macao residents and Taiwan Chinese residents.
You must be able to support yourself without investment returns, work or public assistance in HK.

stay.note: Initial stay normally up to 24 months. Extensions up to 3 years each while you keep the portfolio.

steps: Get a Certifying Proof for the Net Asset Requirement from InvestHK.
Apply to ImmD. If approved in principle you get a visitor visa up to 180 days.
Make the investment and get a Certifying Proof for the Investment Requirements from InvestHK.
Send it to ImmD for final approval.

routes.name: Working Holiday Scheme
routes.summary: Up to 12 months in Hong Kong for ages 18 to 30 from partner countries: Australia, Japan, UK, Korea, France, Sweden, New Zealand, Germany, Canada, Hungary, Ireland, Austria and the Netherlands. Yearly quotas apply, first come first served.

other: Holiday must be your main intention.
Need enough funds, a return ticket or the means to buy one, and insurance for the full stay.
Temporary work only, no permanent jobs. You can only join once.

routes.name: Entry for residence as a dependant
routes.summary: Spouse or civil partner and unmarried children under 18 of people admitted under GEP, ASMTP, IANG, QMAS, TTPS and similar schemes. Hong Kong permanent residents can also sponsor parents aged 60 or over.

other: Sponsor must show a genuine relationship and support you well above subsistence level with suitable housing.
Parents can only be sponsored by permanent residents or residents with no limit of stay.

stay.note: Stay is linked to the sponsor for scheme entrants. For permanent resident sponsors, extensions run 3+3 years for spouse and children, 2+2+3 for parents.

routes.name: Right of abode (permanent residence), non-Chinese
routes.summary: Non-Chinese people who lived in Hong Kong for 7 continuous years right before applying and made it their permanent home can apply for permanent resident status. It is granted only once approved.

other: Enter on a valid travel document and ordinarily reside 7 continuous years.
Declare Hong Kong as your permanent home. Evidence includes habitual residence, family in HK, income and tax payments.

routes.name: Right of abode for Chinese citizens (nationality note)
routes.summary: Chinese citizens born in Hong Kong, or who lived there 7 continuous years, have the right of abode. Chinese nationality rules sit on a separate official page that was not confirmed.

other: Children born outside HK to a Chinese citizen parent with right of abode also qualify, using a Certificate of Entitlement or HKSAR passport.
Dual nationality rules were not confirmed on an official page. Check before applying.

citizenship.note: Right of abode for Chinese citizens, not PRC nationality. Nationality rules not confirmed.
